records.d: The Wright Flyer flew in 1903: powered, controlled flight. Every flying taxi descends from Kitty Hawk. The sky became navigable.
records.h: A 12-horsepower engine drove twin propellers while wing-warping gave control. The flight lasted 12 seconds. Powered flight was proven.
records.mj: Established - documented December 1903 flights; first powered controlled flight.

records.d: Sikorsky's VS-300 flew in 1939: the first practical helicopter. Vertical flight worked. The taxi that needs no runway was imagined.
records.h: A single main rotor with tail-rotor anti-torque gave controlled vertical flight. The configuration became standard. The helicopter was born.
records.mj: Established - documented 1939 first flight; first practical helicopter.

records.d: New York Airways flew helicopter airline service from the 1950s: scheduled rooftop hops between Manhattan and airports. The air taxi existed, with pilots and jet fuel. The business model predates the technology by 70 years.
records.h: Sikorsky helicopters ran scheduled service from Manhattan heliports to area airports. The service was real but loud and costly. The model worked; the machine didn't scale.
records.mj: Established - documented scheduled helicopter airline service; rooftop air taxi.

c: Pan Am Building accident records, May 1977
records.d: In May 1977, a helicopter accident atop the Pan Am Building ended rooftop heliports in Manhattan: the air taxi's first era closed in tragedy. Safety became the industry's founding lesson. The dream waited for better machines.
records.h: Rotor failure on landing killed passengers and a pedestrian, ending rooftop operations. Regulators and insurers retreated. The lesson: urban air service must be far safer than helicopters were.
records.mj: Established - documented May 1977 accident; end of Manhattan rooftop heliports.

records.d: The FAA's 2004 Light Sport Aircraft rule simplified certification for small aircraft: lighter regulation for lighter machines. The regulatory door cracked open. Small electric aircraft gained a path.
records.h: The sport-pilot and LSA framework lowered barriers for simple aircraft. Innovation in small aviation accelerated. The category proved regulators could move.
records.mj: Established - documented 2004 FAA rule; Light Sport Aircraft category.
records.z: timeline|year=2004|span=1|events=FAA LSA rule~small aircraft path opens

records.d: Terrafugia's Transition first flew in 2009: a roadable aircraft, the flying car made real. It was a plane that drove, not a car that flew. The flying car left the cartoon.
records.h: Folding wings let the aircraft drive on roads and fly from runways, certified in light-sport categories. The compromise was real. The concept flew.
k: The flying car leaves the cartoon
records.mj: Established - documented 2009 first flight; roadable aircraft.

records.d: Volocopter's VC1 flew in 2011: the first crewed electric multicopter. Electric vertical flight worked. The eVTOL era's first flight was quiet.
records.h: Eighteen electric rotors lifted a pilot in the multicopter's first crewed flight. Distributed electric propulsion proved itself. The architecture was new.
records.mj: Established - documented 2011 VC1 flight; first crewed electric multicopter.

records.d: Ehang, founded in 2014, bet on autonomous passenger drones: pilotless air taxis from a drone company. The taxi without a pilot was proposed. Autonomy entered the cockpit debate.
records.h: The drone maker pivoted to passenger-grade autonomous multicopters, arguing autonomy simplified certification. The pilot was optional. The industry split on crewed vs. autonomous.
records.mj: Established - documented 2014 founding; autonomous passenger drone bet.

records.d: Ehang unveiled the 184 passenger drone at CES 2016: a one-seat autonomous flyer you summoned like an elevator. The air taxi as appliance. The crowd saw the future board a drone.
records.h: The single-passenger multicopter promised autonomous point-to-point flight with no pilot controls. The interface was a destination. The demo was the product vision.
records.mj: Established - documented January 2016 CES unveiling; passenger drone.

records.d: Uber's Elevate white paper in October 2016 made the business case: on-demand eVTOL networks in cities, with economics. The rideshare giant blessed the air taxi. The industry gained a roadmap.
records.h: The paper modeled urban air mobility demand, vehicle requirements, and infrastructure, catalyzing investment. The vision was quantitative. The roadmap was written.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2016 white paper; urban air mobility vision.
records.z: timeline|year=2016|span=1|events=Uber Elevate white paper~air taxi roadmap written

records.d: Lilium's Eagle flew in April 2017: a ducted-fan electric jet promising 300 km/h cruise. The eVTOL went fast. Speed joined verticality.
records.h: Thirty-six ducted fans in tilting wings lifted the two-seat prototype, transitioning to winged cruise. The jet configuration promised range. The design space widened.
records.mj: Established - documented April 2017 first flight; ducted-fan eVTOL.

records.d: By 2018, eVTOL funding was surging: hundreds of startups and billions in investment chasing the air taxi. The gold rush began. Capital believed.
records.h: Venture and corporate money poured into eVTOL developers worldwide. The field crowded. The race was funded.
records.mj: Emerging - real investment wave; eVTOL funding surge.

records.d: Joby's S4 prototype was flying test campaigns in 2019: a piloted tilt-rotor eVTOL with 150-mile range claims. The serious contender flew. The prototype looked like the product.
records.h: Six tilting propellers transitioned between hover and cruise, with extensive flight testing. The design was mature. The contender was credible.
records.mj: Established - documented test campaigns; Joby S4 prototype.

records.d: Volocopter flew a public test over Singapore's Marina Bay in October 2019: the air taxi demoed in a world city. Regulators watched. The future flew downtown.
records.h: The 2X flew a piloted circuit over the bay with government support. The demonstration was diplomatic. The city saw its skyline's future.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2019 Singapore flight; public eVTOL demo.

records.d: Joby went public via SPAC in August 2020 at a $6.6 billion valuation: the air taxi's Wall Street debut. Public markets priced the dream. The SPAC era funded flight.
records.h: The merger capitalized Joby for certification and production. The valuation was aspirational. The funding was real.
records.mj: Established - documented August 2020 SPAC; $6.6 billion valuation.

records.d: Archer went public via SPAC in February 2021: the air taxi's second Wall Street debut. Competition was capitalized. The race had funding on both sides.
records.h: The merger funded Archer's Midnight development and certification. The field had two funded leaders. The rivalry was financial.
records.mj: Established - documented February 2021 SPAC; Archer public listing.

records.d: The FAA issued Joby a G-1 certification basis: the regulatory path defined. The air taxi gained a rulebook. Certification became a process, not a question.
records.h: The G-1 established the airworthiness standards Joby must meet. The path was formal. The industry watched the precedent.
records.mj: Established - documented FAA G-1 issue; eVTOL certification basis.
records.z: timeline|year=2021|span=1|events=FAA issues G-1 basis~certification path defined

records.d: EASA published vertiport design rules in 2022: the ground infrastructure gained standards. The sky needed parking. The vertiport became real estate.
records.h: Specifications for vertiport dimensions, safety areas, and operations gave cities a template. The infrastructure was specified. The ground caught up.
records.mj: Established - documented 2022 EASA vertiport specifications.

records.d: Joby received its FAA Part 135 air carrier certificate in May 2022: licensed to operate commercial air taxi service. The operator was certified ahead of the aircraft. The company could fly passengers, pending the type certificate.
records.h: The Part 135 certificate authorized on-demand commercial operations. The aircraft certification continued separately. The business was licensed; the machine was pending.
records.mj: Established - documented May 2022 Part 135 certificate; commercial operator approval.

records.d: The FAA issued vertiport design guidance in 2023: American standards for air taxi ground infrastructure. The US template arrived. Cities could plan.
records.h: Engineering Brief guidance specified vertiport geometry and safety for US operations. Planning had a reference. The infrastructure path cleared.
records.mj: Established - documented FAA vertiport engineering guidance.

records.d: By 2023, Eve Air Mobility was advancing certification with ANAC and Embraer's backing: the incumbent's eVTOL. Aviation's establishment joined the race. The startup had a godfather.
records.h: Embraer's experience backed Eve's certification program and production plans. The pedigree mattered. The establishment validated the category.
records.mj: Emerging - real program; Eve certification with Embraer backing.

records.d: Joby signed an agreement for Dubai air taxi service in February 2024: the first commercial market committed. The desert bet on the sky. Launch had a location.
records.h: The agreement with Dubai's RTA targeted 2025-2026 service with vertiports. The commitment was governmental. The market was real.
records.mj: Emerging - real agreement (February 2024); Dubai air taxi service planned.

records.d: Archer advanced Abu Dhabi plans in 2024: the rival's Middle East beachhead. The Gulf became the launchpad. Competition went geographic.
records.h: Agreements for Abu Dhabi operations targeted early service. The region courted both leaders. The launchpad was shared.
records.mj: Emerging - real agreements; Archer Abu Dhabi plans.

records.d: The FAA issued its powered-lift special rule in October 2024: pilot training and operating rules for eVTOLs. The rulebook's final chapter. Pilots could train for the new category.
records.h: The SFAR created the powered-lift category with training and operational requirements. The workforce path opened. The system was nearly complete.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2024 FAA SFAR; powered-lift rules.

records.d: By 2025, eVTOL leaders were deep in FAA certification flight testing: conformity aircraft flying test points. The paperwork was flying. Type certificates approached.
records.h: Piloted conformity aircraft executed certification test campaigns. The data accumulated. The certificate was a matter of test points.
records.mj: Emerging - real testing; eVTOL certification flight campaigns.

records.d: By 2025, first commercial air taxi routes were being announced: airport shuttles and city pairs with vertiports. The network had a first map. Launch was scheduled.
records.h: Operators published initial routes connecting airports to city vertiports. The map was small. The precedent was everything.
records.mj: Emerging - real announcements; first commercial eVTOL routes.
